cards.text: Micah the prophet passes along what the LORD says, and friend, it sounds like a courtroom. Somebody is told to arise and plead a case out loud, and the witnesses being called in aren't even people.

cards.question: The LORD calls on the ___ to hear His case.

cards.text: The mountains are called "you enduring foundations of the earth," and they've been standing there forever. They've seen EVERYTHING, friend. For years, all I saw was the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD's case in front of the mountains is against the nations.

cards.text: The LORD has a case against His own people, and He'll argue it against Israel. The mountains are listening, the hills are listening, and everybody's leaning in for the opening.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD opens His case against His people by reading out a list of their sins.

cards.text: He asks a question instead: "My people, what have I done to you? Testify against Me how I have wearied you!" I bet you could hear a crumb drop.
Then the LORD reminds them He redeemed them from the house of slavery. Friend, He pulled ME out of a junk drawer, and I tell that story to ANYBODY who stands still for five seconds.

cards.question: The LORD says He brought His people up from the land of ___.
Along with Moses, who else does the LORD say He sent before His people?

cards.text: Next, the LORD says to remember Balak, king of Moab, who sent for Balaam, son of Beor, to curse Israel. Balaam blessed them instead, THREE TIMES, and Balak's whole plan came out of the oven upside down (Numbers 22:5-6; 24:10).

Then He says to remember the journey from Shittim to Gilgal, across the Jordan (Joshua 3:1; 4:19). Friend, on most trips the only thing that stops is traffic, but on THAT trip the Jordan stopped (Joshua 3:16).

cards.question: Why does the LORD want His people to remember Balaam and the journey to Gilgal?

answers.text: So they'll see the LORD has been righteous
So they'll fear the kings around them
So they'll miss their old days in Egypt

cards.text: Now a new voice. Someone asks, "With what shall I come before the LORD when I bow before the God on high?"

cards.question: What's the first gift this person wonders about bringing before the LORD?

answers.text: Gold and silver from the treasury

cards.text: Then the questions get BIGGER: would the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, or ten thousand rivers of oil? Friend, I tossed one extra scoop of chocolate chips in a batch once and walked around all week like a HERO.

cards.question: True or false: the person even wonders about giving his firstborn for his sin.

cards.text: Then the answer comes, plain and simple: "He has shown you, O man, what is good."

cards.question: So what does the LORD require?

answers.text: Justice and mercy and a humble walk with Him
Bigger offerings brought at every single feast
A long trip up to the temple every year

cards.question: The LORD requires you to act ___, to love ___, and to walk humbly with your God.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "The mountains are called ... forever." / "They've seen EVERYTHING, friend." / "For years, all I saw was the back of a junk drawer."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says the mountains have "been standing there forever" as a fact. Micah 6:2 only calls them "enduring foundations of the earth." Saying "forever" goes further than the text. The exaggeration belongs in the joke line, not in the retelling.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Moses first appears in this card's question, but nothing says who he is. Card 8 left him out.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke "Balak's whole plan came out of the oven upside down" doesn't click. A cookie coming out upside down isn't a known picture of something going wrong, so the image doesn't match a plan that backfires into a blessing. A baker would need it explained.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "So they'll miss their old days in Egypt" isn't believable. These verses have just told how the LORD redeemed them from the house of slavery and turned Balaam's curse into blessing, so wanting them to miss Egypt makes no sense. "So they'll fear the kings around them" is also weak. Both make the right answer stand out.

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.
